editorial:
Imagine getting out of prison after five years and wanting nothing more than a quiet life, only to find out your best friend left you with a mountain of debt to a scary mobster. That is exactly what happens to Chance. You get to see him struggle between the man he wants to be and the criminal world he was born into. The tension is high because his father is actually a leader of a white supremacist gang in prison, which adds a heavy layer of family drama to the whole story. Along the way, he meets Pearl, and their relationship gives you a reason to root for him to actually make it out of the gutter.

What really makes this work is the acting, especially from Ed Harris and Taraji P. Henson, who bring a lot of weight to their roles. The action scenes are gritty and the pacing keeps you moving, though some parts of the plot feel a bit predictable. If you enjoy crime stories about redemption, you will definitely like this one. You should check if it is available for renting on Apple TV or maybe grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see all the detail in the fight scenes.
endingExplained: In the final act, Chance has to face the violence he tried to leave behind. He fights to protect Pearl and break free from the mobsters and the shadow of his father. After a series of brutal confrontations, he manages to settle the debts and cut ties with the criminals. He chooses love and a clean slate over the cycle of hate his father represents, finally finding the peace and freedom he wanted since the start.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gritty crime stories and movies about breaking away from a bad family history.
